findings.issue: OpenMath binds P,Q as sets plus a dummy element a and writes (in a P); Lean has P Q : Prop, so the OM states a pointwise membership statement for arbitrary sets, not the propositional law. Use a propositional-truth symbol (needs vocab entry proposition_holds: args [term], returns prop, meaning 'the proposition P is true').

patch.openmath: (forall (P Q) (<-> (-> (proposition_holds P) (proposition_holds Q)) (-> (not (proposition_holds Q)) (not (proposition_holds P)))))

findings.issue: Same hack as contrapositive_iff: propositions encoded as (in a P) with a dummy element a. Use proposition_holds (new vocab symbol, args [term], returns prop).

patch.openmath: (forall (P Q) (and (<-> (not (and (proposition_holds P) (proposition_holds Q))) (or (not (proposition_holds P)) (not (proposition_holds Q)))) (<-> (not (or (proposition_holds P) (proposition_holds Q))) (and (not (proposition_holds P)) (not (proposition_holds Q))))))

findings.issue: Carrier type alpha is dropped: x is quantified over everything and the predicate is a set P (in x P). Add an explicit carrier A and use holds_at (already in school_data_logic vocab) so ranges are bounded and predicate encoding is consistent with the school_data_logic cards.

patch.openmath: (forall (A P) (<-> (not (forall (x) (-> (in x A) (holds_at P x)))) (exists (x) (and (in x A) (not (holds_at P x))))))

findings.issue: Same carrier-dropping / predicate-as-set encoding as not_forall_iff_exists_not.

patch.openmath: (forall (A P) (<-> (not (exists (x) (and (in x A) (holds_at P x)))) (forall (x) (-> (in x A) (not (holds_at P x))))))

findings.issue: alpha and beta are not in the OM: x and y range over everything. In Lean the outer y must lie in beta (which may differ in emptiness from alpha), so carriers matter. Add A,B guards.

patch.openmath: (forall (A B R) (-> (exists (y) (and (in y B) (forall (x) (-> (in x A) (relates R x y))))) (forall (x) (-> (in x A) (exists (y) (and (in y B) (relates R x y)))))))

findings.issue: complement has no ambient set and indexed_union/indexed_inter (lambda only) do not carry the index set, so the empty-index case and the ambient type are invisible. Prefer indexed_union/indexed_inter with args [term, term_function] (index set, family) and setdiff X (...) with an explicit ambient X; note intersection over an empty index set must be defined as X in the vocabulary meaning.
No map_between/carrier guards: x and y range over everything and f,g,h are untyped, so domain/codomain information that the Lean statement carries is erased.

patch.openmath: (forall (A B f g h) (-> (and (map_between f A B) (map_between g B A) (map_between h B A) (forall (x) (-> (in x A) (= (fn_value g (fn_value f x)) x))) (forall (y) (-> (in y B) (= (fn_value f (fn_value h y)) y)))) (= g h)))

findings.issue: indexed_union takes only a lambda, so the index set I never appears in the union: the OM unions A_i over an unspecified index range while I is used only as a guard on i. Read literally the OM allows i outside I with unconstrained A_i, or equally the same OM would be produced for the false 'arbitrary index set' variant (the hard_negative) once the guard is dropped. The index set must be an argument of indexed_union (change vocab to args [term, term_function]; indexed_de_morgan must change in step).

patch.openmath: (forall (I A) (-> (and (countable I) (forall (i) (-> (in i I) (countable (fn_value A i))))) (countable (indexed_union I (lambda (i) (fn_value A i))))))

findings.issue: Answer shows no surjection N->R exists and then concludes |N|<|R| without saying why that suffices (|R|<=|N| gives an injection R->N and hence, as R is nonempty, a surjection N->R). One-sentence gap.

patch.answer:
自然数全体$\mathbb{N}$と実数全体$\mathbb{R}$の濃度を比べる。
$\mathbb{N}\subseteq\mathbb{R}$より$|\mathbb{N}|\leq|\mathbb{R}|$なので、全射$\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$がないことを示せばよい（$|\mathbb{R}|\leq|\mathbb{N}|$なら単射$\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{N}$があり、$\mathbb{R}$は空でないのでその左逆写像から全射$\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$が得られるため）。実数列$(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$を任意にとる。
閉区間の列$I_0\supseteq I_1\supseteq\cdots$を、長さが正で$x_n\notin I_n$となるように順に選ぶ。$I_{-1}=[0,1]$とする。$I_{n-1}=[a,b]$（$a<b$）まで定まったとき、$[a,a+(b-a)/3]$と$[b-(b-a)/3,b]$は交わらないので、少なくとも一方は$x_n$を含まない。その一方を$I_n$とする。
実数の完備性（区間縮小法）により、$\bigcap_n I_n$は空でない。その元は$x_n\notin I_n$よりどの$x_n$とも異なる。よって$n\mapsto x_n$は全射でなく、$|\mathbb{N}|<|\mathbb{R}|$である。

findings.issue: Japanese statement 「$k\leq n$の全ての$n$で$P(n)$ならば$P(n+1)$」 can be read as 'if P holds for all n>=k then P(n+1)'; Lean is (forall n>=k, P n -> P (n+1)). Hard negative counterexample (P(n) := n>=k, fails below k) needs k>=1; for k=0 the claim is true.

patch.statement: 自然数$k$と自然数上の述語$P$について、$P(k)$が成り立ち、かつ$k\leq n$を満たす全ての$n$について「$P(n)$ならば$P(n+1)$」が成り立つならば、$k\leq n$を満たす全ての$n$で$P(n)$が成り立つ。

hard_negative.statement: 同じ仮定のもとで、全ての自然数$n$（$k$未満も含む）で$P(n)$が成り立つ。
hard_negative.reason: $k$未満の$n$については何も言えない。$k\geq1$のとき、$P(n)$を「$n\geq k$」とすると仮定は成り立つが、$P(0)$は偽である。

findings.issue: (+ b 1) uses arith1 plus for ordinal successor; arith1.plus is commutative, ordinal addition is not. Use a dedicated ordinal_add (or ordinal_succ) symbol.

patch.openmath: (forall (a) (-> (is_ordinal a) (or (= a 0) (exists (b) (and (is_ordinal b) (= a (ordinal_add b 1)))) (limit_ordinal a))))

findings.issue: The OM asserts (= (+ 1 omega) omega) and (!= (+ omega 1) omega) with arith1 plus, which the CD declares commutative: read with standard OpenMath semantics the encoding is self-contradictory, and retrieval cannot tell ordinal from numeric addition. Introduce ordinal_add (non-commutative) and use it; likewise carriers for 1.

patch.openmath: (and (= (ordinal_add 1 omega_ordinal) omega_ordinal) (!= (ordinal_add omega_ordinal 1) omega_ordinal))

findings.issue: Cardinal sum/product encoded with arith1 + and *, guarded only by is_cardinal; a statement a+b=max(a,b) with arith1 symbols looks false in numeric arithmetic. Dedicated cardinal_add / cardinal_mul symbols (or carrier-tagged) would avoid wrong reuse.

patch.openmath: (forall (a b) (-> (and (is_cardinal a) (is_cardinal b) (<= aleph_zero a) (<= aleph_zero b)) (and (-> (<= a b) (and (= (cardinal_add a b) b) (= (cardinal_mul a b) b))) (-> (<= b a) (and (= (cardinal_add a b) a) (= (cardinal_mul a b) a))))))

findings.issue: Cardinal power laws written with arith1 ^, +, *: a^(b+c)=a^b*a^c is a numeric identity too, but a^(b*c)=(a^b)^c etc. are retrieved for numbers and cardinals alike; add cardinal_pow/cardinal_add/cardinal_mul so the carrier is explicit (Lean statement is for Cardinal only).

patch.openmath: (forall (a b c) (-> (and (is_cardinal a) (is_cardinal b) (is_cardinal c)) (and (= (cardinal_pow a (cardinal_add b c)) (cardinal_mul (cardinal_pow a b) (cardinal_pow a c))) (= (cardinal_pow a (cardinal_mul b c)) (cardinal_pow (cardinal_pow a b) c)) (= (cardinal_pow (cardinal_mul a b) c) (cardinal_mul (cardinal_pow a c) (cardinal_pow b c))))))

patch.answer:
$e$を自然対数の底、$\pi$を円周率とする。$x>0$、$x\neq 1$では$\log x<x-1$である。実際、$f(x)=x-1-\log x$は$f^{\prime}(x)=1-\dfrac{1}{x}$より$x=1$でのみ最小値$0$をとる。
$e=\sum_{k\geq 0}\dfrac{1}{k!}$で、$k\geq 2$では$k!\geq 2^{k-1}$（$k\geq 3$では真に大きい）なので$e<1+1+\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{4}+\cdots=3$である。また円に内接する正六角形の周の長さ$6$は円周$2\pi$より短いので$\pi>3$である。よって$e<3<\pi$であり、$\dfrac{\pi}{e}\neq 1$なので、$x=\dfrac{\pi}{e}$を代入すると$\log\pi-1<\dfrac{\pi}{e}-1$、すなわち$e\log\pi<\pi$を得る。指数関数は増加関数なので、$\pi^e=\exp(e\log\pi)<\exp(\pi)=e^\pi$である。

Learner-facing answer writes the false congruence 『$1+1\equiv 1\pmod 3$』 as the contradiction; the correct statement is a^2+b^2 = 2 (mod 3) versus c^2 = 1 (mod 3). Rest of the proof (mod 5, mod 4 cases, coprimality) is correct and complete.

patch.answer:
$a,b,c$を$a^2+b^2=c^2$をみたす整数とする。$3,4,5$が$abc$を割り切ることを順に示す。
$3$で割り切れない整数の平方は$3$を法として$1$である。$a,b,c$がどれも$3$で割り切れないと左辺は$1+1\equiv 2\pmod 3$、右辺は$c^2\equiv 1\pmod 3$となって合わないので、$3$は$abc$を割り切る。
$5$で割り切れない整数の平方は$5$を法として$\pm 1$である。$a,b,c$がどれも$5$で割り切れないと、左辺は$5$を法として$0$か$\pm 2$であり、$c^2\equiv\pm 1$に合わない。よって$5$は$abc$を割り切る。
$a,b$がともに奇数なら$c^2\equiv 2\pmod 4$となり不合理である。$a,b$がともに偶数なら$4$は$ab$を割り切る。一方だけが偶数の場合、対称性より$a$を偶数として$b,c$は奇数である。奇数の平方は$8$を法として$1$なので$a^2=c^2-b^2\equiv 0\pmod 8$であり、$4$は$a$を割り切る。いずれの場合も$4$は$abc$を割り切る。
$3,4,5$は互いに素なので、$60$は$abc$を割り切る。

systemic: OpenMath encodes propositional and predicate variables inconsistently: propositions as (in a P) with a dummy element, predicates as sets with unbounded x, elsewhere holds_at/relates; carriers (alpha, beta) are dropped. Proposed fix: vocab symbol proposition_holds (args [term]) for Prop variables, and holds_at/relates always with an explicit carrier guard.

Overloaded arith1 symbols (+, *, ^) are reused for ordinals and cardinals without carrier info (ordinal_add_not_commutative asserts 1+w=w and w+1!=w with a commutative CD symbol); indexed_union/indexed_inter take only a lambda and so lose the index set (countable_union_of_countable is unfaithful). Use ordinal_add, cardinal_add/mul/pow and indexed_union with args [term, term_function].
Finiteness is encoded as (in (size s) N) in all 20 school_data_logic data/counting cards; use the reusable finite_set concept instead.

All 43 entrance_exam cards are kind=textbook, level=1 (undergraduate year), though the problems are high-school level (should be level high) and none is gap; the statement field is a question or imperative in 14 of them (patched). Mathematics was verified: every claimed identity, bound and finite table (Euler n^2+n+41 mod p for p=3..37, 2^a/3^b counts, 22/7-pi polynomial identity) checks out, and no Lean junk-value dependence was found (all divisions have positivity side conditions, ℕ-subtraction cases are safe, counts are stated additively).
